questions.problem: Find the real solutions to the equation $5\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=5.$
questions.worked_solution:
The definitions of $\operatorname{cosh}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{sinh}⁡x$ are

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}),\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}).
$$

Substituting the above definitions into the equation  $5\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot (\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}))-\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}) & =5 \\ \frac{5}{2}{e}^{x}+\frac{5}{2}{e}^{-x}-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{x}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x} & =5 \\ 2{e}^{x}+3{e}^{-x} & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we multiply both sides of the equation by ${e}^{x},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}\cdot (2{e}^{x}+3{e}^{-x}) & ={e}^{x}\cdot 5 \\ 2{e}^{2x}+3 & =5{e}^{x} \\ 2{e}^{2x}-5{e}^{x}+3 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

This is a quadratic equation in ${e}^{x}$ that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2{e}^{x}-3)({e}^{x}-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

By the zero-product property, we have to solve two equations:

$$
2{e}^{x}-3=0,\,{e}^{x}-1=0
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{e}^{x}-3 & =0 &  & \, & {e}^{x}-1 & =0 \\ {e}^{x} & =\frac{3}{2} &  & \, & {e}^{x} & =1 \\ {e}^{x} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{2}) &  & \, & x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡1=0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=0$ and $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{2})$ are the real solutions to the equation.

questions.problem: Find the real solution to the equation $5\operatorname{tanh}⁡x=4.$
questions.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{tanh}⁡x$ is

$$
\operatorname{tanh}⁡x=\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}}.
$$

Substituting the above definition into the equation $5\operatorname{tanh}⁡x=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot (\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}}) & =4 \\ 5({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}) & =4({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}) \\ 5{e}^{x}-5{e}^{-x} & =4{e}^{x}+4{e}^{-x} \\ {e}^{x} & =9{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we multiply both sides of the equation by ${e}^{x}$ and solve the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}\cdot {e}^{x} & ={e}^{x}\cdot 9{e}^{-x} \\ {e}^{2x} & =9 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡9 \\ 2x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡9 \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡9 \\ x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{1/2}) \\ x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the only real solution is $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡3.$

The definitions of $\operatorname{cosh}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{sinh}⁡x$ are

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}),\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}).
$$

Substituting the above definitions into the equation $\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=7,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x})+\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}) & =7 \\ \frac{1}{2}{e}^{x}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{x}-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x} & =7 \\ {e}^{x} & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x} & =7 \\ x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)$ is the only real solution to the equation.

questions.worked_solution:
The definitions of $\operatorname{cosh}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{sinh}⁡x$ are

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}),\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}).
$$

Substituting the above definitions into the equation $\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+5\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x})+5\cdot (\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})) & =5 \\ \frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x})+\frac{5}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}) & =5 \\ \frac{1}{2}{e}^{x}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x}+\frac{5}{2}{e}^{x}-\frac{5}{2}{e}^{-x} & =5 \\ 3{e}^{x}-2{e}^{-x} & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we multiply both sides of the equation by ${e}^{x},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}\cdot (3{e}^{x}-2{e}^{-x}) & ={e}^{x}\cdot 5 \\ 3{e}^{2x}-2 & =5{e}^{x} \\ 3{e}^{2x}-5{e}^{x}-2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a quadratic equation in ${e}^{x}$ that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3{e}^{x}+1)({e}^{x}-2) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

By the zero-product property, we have to solve two equations:

$$
3{e}^{x}+1=0,\,{e}^{x}-2=0.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{e}^{x}+1 & =0 &  & \, & {e}^{x}-2 & =0 \\ 3{e}^{x} & =-1 &  & \, & {e}^{x} & =2 \\ {e}^{x} & =-\frac{1}{3} &  & \, & x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2).\end{aligned}
$$

There are no real values of $x$ for which ${e}^{x}=-\frac{1}{3}.$ Therefore, the only real solution to the equation is

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2).
$$
